content: Signature 1932 is a premium, hand-crafted cigar brand owned by the Padilla Cigar Company, based in Hialeah, Florida. This brand was developed by José Pepin Garcia and is primarily produced at the El Rey de los Habanos factory, located in the Little Havana neighborhood of Miami, Florida. However, one specific size, known as La Perla, is manufactured at Tabacalera Cubana S.A. (TACUBA), Pepin's factory in Estelí, Nicaragua. The brand was named as a tribute to Heberto Padilla, a renowned Cuban poet born in 1932, by his son Ernesto Padilla, the owner of Padilla Cigars. The release of the Signature 1932 line was carried out in phases. The initial three sizes—Robusto, Churchill, and Torpedo—were launched in October 2006. These cigars were presented in a distinctive cedar box containing 45 cigars (15 of each size), with only 500 such boxes produced. These boxes were designed to serve as permanent display pieces, intended to be refilled with subsequent shipments. The second phase of the release began in January 2007 with the introduction of the Toro size. This was followed in February 2007 by the Lancero size and a second release of the previously launched sizes, all packaged in Cuban-style boxes containing 25 cigars. The final size, La Perla, was delayed and eventually released in late March or early April 2007. This marked the transition to the regular production phase of the brand. The Signature 1932 line has received notable recognition and accolades. The Churchill size was awarded a rating of 90 in the December 2006 issue of Cigar Aficionado magazine and was ranked as the 14th best cigar of 2006 by the same publication. Additionally, the Churchill was named Cigar of the Week for the week of January 20, 2007. The Robusto size received a rating of 88 in the February 2007 issue of Cigar Aficionado. The La Perla size achieved a rating of 90 in the May 8, 2007, issue of Cigar Insider. The Signature 1932 line consists of six different sizes, or vitolas. The cigars feature a Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper, with Nicaraguan Criollo used for both the filler and binder. They are packaged in Cuban-style boxes containing 25 cigars. The La Perla size is unique within the line, as it is the smallest size, comes unbanded, and is packaged in cabinets of 50 cigars. Its production is limited, and it is the only size manufactured in Nicaragua at TACUBA. The cigar band of the Signature 1932 is a highly intricate and artistic design. It features a maroon background with elaborate gold borders and scrollwork. On the left side of the band, the words Little Havana Miami are inscribed in gold. The right side includes an ornate P monogram and the words Cuban Crafted, along with a lot number, all in gold. The center of the band prominently displays the Padilla monogram at the top, followed by the word Padilla, then Signature in script, and finally 1932. At the bottom of the band, the Cuban coat of arms is depicted.
